_comment: Illustrative reverse-impact example. Synthetic subject and figures. Note the three separate tables: the ranked union, additive dollars, and re-attribution which must never be added.

groups.name: Money market A
groups.note: Union across the market, its oracle and its admin set: the same underlying position

deps.name: Market admin, threshold 4 with a 48h timelock

groups.name: Money market B
groups.note: Multi-collateral pool, pro-rated at the subject's 47.8% share of the market's collateral

groups.name: AMM pools
groups.note: LP loss is the whole pool, not the subject's leg: a worthless asset is arbitraged against the paired asset. Applies to AMMs only

groups.name: Bridges
groups.note: Bridged representations of the subject on other chains

groups.name: Positions below the floor, carried as one aggregate
groups.note: Everything under 0.1% of the denominator, kept in the total rather than dropped

additive.note: isolated market, bad debt equals the amount borrowed against the subject
paired asset, denominated in something other than the subject

additive.path: Money market A borrow ceiling against this collateral
additive.note: ceiling, not a measurement: the drawn amount against this specific collateral is not exposed by the protocol

reattribution.layer: Receipt tokens over the same deposits
reattribution.resolves: holders of the money markets' receipt tokens, the same dollars as the ranked table
vault depositors, whose loss is already inside the money market rows above
holders of the bridged representation, the same dollars as the bridge row

backing_exposure.basis: collateral-backed debt summed across all controllers, not total supply
collateral-backed debt across all controllers. At this share the path propagates at close to full value
